name: date
summary: Prints or formats the date and time.
description: Without an argument, prints the current date and time. An argument starting with + sets the format: %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day), %H:%M:%S (time), %s (seconds since 1970, the “Unix timestamp”). Widely used in scripts to name backup files. Changing the system time requires sudo; timedatectl is usually used instead.

options.description: Prints a date other than now: "tomorrow", "2 days ago", "2024-12-25", "@1700000000" (timestamp).
Prints UTC time instead of local time.
Prints the last modification date of a file.

examples.explanation: US-style format; the quotes protect the space. In a script, $(date +%F) inserts today’s date into a file name.
The Unix timestamp: seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970.
